replayr

replayr imports emulator input recordings into R for analysis. It reads buttons, keyboard keys, analogue sticks, mouse movement, touch, and motion sensors, together with recording metadata and timing information.

Formats and platforms

The package reads 34 recording formats from BizHawk, Dolphin, FCEUX, libTAS, Mupen64, Snes9x, openMSX, and other recording tools. Supported platforms include:

Family Platforms
Arcade and application platforms Adobe Flash; Android; Arcade; IBM PC compatible; IBM PC DOS; Java 2 Platform, Micro Edition (J2ME); Mac OS / macOS; PICO-8; TIC-80; Web.
Atari Atari 2600; Atari 7800; Atari Jaguar; Atari Jaguar CD; Atari Lynx.
Home computers and calculators Amiga; Apple II; Commodore 64; MSX Home Computer System; Spectravideo SVI-318/328; Texas Instruments TI-83 Series; ZX Spectrum.
NEC NEC PC-98; PC Engine / TurboGrafx-16; PC Engine CD / TurboGrafx-CD; PC-FX; SuperGrafx.
Nintendo Famicom Disk System; Game Boy; Game Boy Advance; Game Boy Color; Nintendo 3DS; Nintendo 64; Nintendo 64DD; Nintendo DS; Nintendo DSi; Nintendo Entertainment System / Famicom; Nintendo GameCube; Satellaview; Super Game Boy; Super Nintendo / Super Famicom; Virtual Boy; Wii.
Other consoles 3DO; CD-i; ColecoVision; Fairchild Channel F; Intellivision; Neo Geo Pocket; Odyssey 2 / Videopac; Sony PlayStation; Uzebox; Vectrex; WonderSwan.
Sega Game Gear; Sega 32X; Sega CD / Mega-CD; Sega Genesis / Mega Drive; Sega Master System; Sega Saturn; Sega SG-1000.

The compatibility catalogue lists each format, version, controller variant, and platform combination. Some desktop and browser games use input recorded through a host application such as libTAS or Hourglass; the catalogue identifies these cases. It is also included in the installed package: vignette("compatibility", package = "replayr").

Getting started

Install from a local source checkout:

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_local("path/to/replayr")

Read a recording and summarise the use of one controller:

library(replayr)

path <- system.file("extdata", "paper", "hold.fm2", package = "replayr")
movie <- read_movie(path)
input <- player(movie, 1L)
sort(colMeans(input), decreasing = TRUE)  # Proportion held

read_movie() chooses the reader from the file extension. player() returns a logical matrix with observations in rows and controls in columns. A TRUE value means that the control is active. The example file contains sustained Right and B input with brief A presses. Package examples are original artificial recordings.

Controllers and analogue input

Each recording has compact columns for its controls. Shared identifiers make comparable controls match across devices; button_layout(movie) gives the mapping, and align_buttons() aligns matrices from several recordings.

See the universal controller layout for the shared identifiers.

Recorded numeric values are available through analog_channels(). Stick input can additionally be represented as four or eight directions, an angle, or an angle with magnitude. Choose a representation for each stick:

path <- system.file("extdata", "sample.dtm", package = "replayr")
movie <- read_movie(path,
  analog = c(left = "angle+magnitude", right = "cardinal8"))

The original coordinates remain available. Mouse, touch, light-gun, and motion values retain the units supplied by their recording format.

Rows follow the source recording: they may be frames, controller polls, or timestamped events. n_frames() counts imported observations. Readers retain available timing information and identify polls whose controller port is unknown, so these distinctions can be handled in an analysis.

Documentation

Open vignette("replayr", package = "replayr") for examples of button summaries, controller alignment, mouse movement, and Wii motion. Reader help pages describe format-specific options; ?read_bk2_chunks explains how to process large BK2 recordings in chunks.
